key_insight: A Lagrangian, particle-based view of heat transport can expose coherent transport routes and finite-time attracting/repelling structures that standard Eulerian temperature fields hide.
engineering_relevance: This helps engineers diagnose where heat actually moves in unsteady convection, improving interpretation of cooling performance and thermal design decisions.
method: Advect massless particles through a time-reparameterized spacetime formulation of thermal transport.
Accumulate path contributions to visualize coherent heat transport pathways.
Extract finite-time attracting and repelling structures from aperiodic, non-conservative heat transfer.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a visualization technique for unsteady heat transfer and argues that it reveals structures and routes not visible with conventional Eulerian temperature visualization.
watch_item: Because heat transport is aperiodic and non-conservative, the method may require careful time reparameterization and may be sensitive to trajectory integration choices.
paper_title: Visualizing Lagrangian Heat Transport Paths and Density Structures in Unsteady Heat Transfer
